## Tall Q5_K GEMVs faster on iGPUs without XMX

- **On iGPUs without XMX** (Core Ultra Meteor Lake and Arrow Lake-S, Iris Xe, UHD), generation's tall Q5_K matrices read their weights straight into registers. "Tall" means at least 8,192 rows and at least twice as many rows as columns, as in the gate / up / q of the Qwen3.5 4B and 9B UD-Q4_K_XL files. On a Core Ultra 5 125H those matrices are 7-10 % faster. The 9B generates 0.7 % faster (12.38 -> 12.47 tok/s), and the 4B is within noise. The output is the same bit for bit (checked on both models). Discrete cards and iGPUs with XMX are unchanged, and so are two-pass models (Gemma 4, Qwen3 dense) and MoE experts. `ARC_GV_K4=0` turns it off.
- **`ARC_PROF_GVTYPE=1`**: `--prof-gen` splits each generation GEMV's row by weight type (`gemm_gate Q4_K`, `gemm_gate Q5_K`).

**Please test on your machine** if you have an Intel iGPU without XMX: a Core Ultra 100-series (Meteor Lake), a Core Ultra 200S desktop (Arrow Lake-S), or an Iris Xe / UHD laptop or desktop. Paste the output into an issue. Use any of these models: Qwen3.5-4B or 9B UD-Q4_K_XL, or another Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL dense model, such as a 27B. The runs compare the new choice with the old one, twice each, in this order.

Windows (PowerShell, in the inferzero folder):

```
$m = "<path to the .gguf>"
foreach ($k in "off", "on", "on", "off") { if ($k -eq "on") { Remove-Item Env:ARC_GV_K4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } else { $env:ARC_GV_K4 = "0" }; "== new choice $k"; .\bin\runz.exe $m --bench-pp 512 --n 128 2>&1 | Select-String "^tg128|tg steps" }
Remove-Item Env:ARC_GV_K4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$env:ARC_PROF_GVTYPE = "1"; .\bin\runz.exe $m --bench-pp 512 --n 64 --prof-gen 2>&1 | Select-String "Q5_K|^tg64"
```

Linux:

```
m=<path to the .gguf>
for k in off on on off; do echo "== new choice $k"; if [ $k = off ]; then e="ARC_GV_K4=0"; else e=""; fi; env $e ./bin/runz "$m" --bench-pp 512 --n 128 2>&1 | grep -E "^tg128|tg steps"; done
ARC_PROF_GVTYPE=1 ./bin/runz "$m" --bench-pp 512 --n 64 --prof-gen 2>&1 | grep -E "Q5_K|^tg64"
```

Say which CPU / GPU and which model you ran.
